questions.question: For resistors connected in series, the quantity that is the SAME through each resistor is:
A 6 Ω and a 3 Ω resistor are connected in parallel. Their combined resistance is:
Adding another resistor in parallel to an existing network always:
options: Decreases the total resistance, because a new branch is a new path for current

questions.question: A useful check on any parallel-combination answer is that it must be:
options: Larger than the largest branch resistance
Equal to the average of the branches
Equal to the sum of the branches
Smaller than the smallest branch resistance

questions.question: The emf of a battery is best defined as:
options: The voltage across the external resistor
The heat generated inside the battery
The total energy the battery transfers to each coulomb of charge
The current the battery can deliver

questions.question: A 12 V battery with internal resistance 0,5 Ω drives a 5,5 Ω external resistor. The current is:
In that same circuit, the terminal voltage while the current flows is:
A voltmeter across a battery reads the full emf only when:
options: The external resistance is very small
The current is at its maximum
No current flows, so the lost volts Ir are zero

questions.question: A 24 V battery (r = 1 Ω) feeds a 5 Ω resistor in series with a parallel pair of 6 Ω and 3 Ω. The main current is:
In that circuit, the voltage across the parallel pair is:
With 6 V across the pair, the currents through the 6 Ω and 3 Ω branches are:
options: 1 A and 2 A — and they add to the main current of 3 A

questions.question: The recommended routine for a network with internal resistance is:
options: Guess the branch currents first, then find the emf
Ignore the internal resistance until the last step
Work only with power values throughout
Collapse the external network, solve the whole loop for the main current, then split voltages and currents branch by branch

questions.question: On a graph of terminal voltage against current for a battery, the vertical intercept and gradient give:
options: Intercept: the emf; gradient: negative the internal resistance
Intercept: the internal resistance; gradient: the emf
Intercept: the terminal voltage; gradient: the power
Intercept: zero; gradient: the external resistance

questions.question: When an extra bulb is connected in parallel to a battery with internal resistance, the terminal voltage:
options: Rises, because there is more resistance
Drops, because the total current rises and the lost volts Ir increase

questions.question: In the 24 V circuit with a main current of 3 A, the power dissipated in the 5 Ω resistor is:
The power wasted inside that battery (r = 1 Ω, I = 3 A) is:
In the pump picture, the emf is the promise and the terminal voltage is:
options: The toll paid inside the pump
The promise minus the toll — what is actually delivered at the terminals

questions.question: The internal toll of a battery is zero whenever:
options: No current flows through the battery

questions.question: An old torch battery reads a healthy voltage on a voltmeter but barely lights the torch. The best explanation is:
options: Its internal resistance has grown large, so most of the emf is lost inside once current flows
The bulb has become more resistive

questions.question: In the river picture, resistors in series are like:
options: Rapids one after another on the same river — every drop passes through all of them

questions.question: Adding a narrow extra channel around the island makes the total flow:
options: Easier — any new channel carries water that previously had to queue elsewhere
Harder, because narrow channels resist strongly

questions.question: Series and parallel arrangements share quantities differently. The correct pairing is:
options: Series shares current equally by value; parallel shares voltage by value
Series: same current, voltages divide; parallel: same voltage, currents divide

questions.question: Household appliances are wired in parallel so that:
options: The total resistance stays as large as possible
Each one feels the full supply voltage and draws its own current independently
The current through each is identical

questions.question: The starter motor dims the headlights because it is:
options: A series resistor that blocks the lamps
A device that raises the battery's emf
A switch that disconnects the lamps
A hungry low-resistance parallel branch that makes the total current surge

questions.question: The four-link explanation chain, in the correct order, is:
options: Current rises — resistance falls — toll falls — voltage rises
External resistance falls — total current rises — lost volts Ir rise — terminal voltage drops
Terminal voltage drops — current rises — resistance falls — toll rises
Emf falls — current falls — resistance rises — voltage rises

questions.question: A battery that reads 12 V idle but collapses under cranking load most likely has:
options: A high internal resistance from aged chemistry

questions.question: Overloading one multiplug weakens every appliance on it because each added device:
options: Opens another parallel branch, raising the total current and the volts lost along the supply
